The Queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon (1 Kgs 10:1-13) became legendary for its display of wealth, wisdom, and spice caravans. Prophetically, Sheba represents distant commercial splendor: its traders deal in gold (Ps 72:15), frankincense (Jer 6:20), and precious stones (Ezek 27:22). Isaiah envisions Sheba's caravans streaming to Jerusalem in eschatological pilgrimage (Isa 60:6). Job's 'caravans of Sheba' symbolize dashed expectations in the desert (Job 6:19). The genealogies trace Sheba through both Hamitic (Gen 10:7) and Semitic (Gen 10:28; 25:3) lines, reflecting the complex ethnic landscape of ancient Arabia."
